seo.title: Craft Beer in Amsterdam (2026) | tabiji.ai
seo.metaDescription: Discover the best craft beer in Amsterdam for 2026 — curated picks with maps, hours, and insider tips.

hero.subtitle: Amsterdam's craft beer scene has exploded, moving beyond traditional lagers to embrace innovative breweries and cozy taprooms serving a diverse range of styles.

picks.name: 1Brouwerij 't IJ
picks.whyItMadeTheList: Located beside the iconic De Gooyer windmill, Brouwerij 't IJ is Amsterdam's most famous craft brewery. It offers a lively atmosphere, an outdoor terrace perfect for sunny days, and a range of organic, unfiltered beers that are staples in many Amsterdam bars. Their tasting room is a must-visit for classic Dutch craft.
picks.insiderTip: They also have a smaller, less crowded taproom called 't Blauwe Theehuis in Vondelpark for a more relaxed setting.
picks.redditQuote: “You absolutely HAVE to go to Brouwerij 't IJ. The windmill, the vibe, and Zatte... it's just pure Amsterdam.”
picks.mapQuery: Brouwerij 't IJ, Funenkade 7, 1018 AL Amsterdam, Netherlands

picks.name: 2Oedipus Brewing Taproom
picks.whyItMadeTheList: Oedipus Brewing is known for its bold flavors, colorful branding, and a fantastic taproom in Amsterdam-Noord. Their space is bright, often hosts DJs or events, and features an ever-changing lineup of inventive beers. A rotation of food trucks ensures you'll always find a delicious pairing.
picks.insiderTip: Take the free ferry from Central Station to NDSM-Werf, then it's a short walk or bike ride. Combine it with exploring the creative Noord district.
picks.redditQuote: “Oedipus is such a fun spot, great music, wild beers, and the food truck game is always on point. Definitely worth the trip to Noord.”
picks.mapQuery: Oedipus Brewing, Schaafstraat 21, 1021 KD Amsterdam, Netherlands

picks.name: 3Craft & Draft
picks.whyItMadeTheList: Nestled in the bustling De Pijp district, Craft & Draft boasts an impressive 40 taps featuring a constantly rotating selection of local, national, and international craft beers. The knowledgeable staff can guide you through their diverse offerings, making it a paradise for any serious beer connoisseur.
picks.whatToOrder: Ask for a flight of their latest unique guest taps
picks.insiderTip: Their menu on Untappd is usually updated in real-time, so you can check what's on tap before you go.
picks.redditQuote: “Craft & Draft is my go-to for variety. Seriously, 40 taps, they always have something new and exciting. Staff know their stuff too!”
picks.mapQuery: Craft & Draft, Overtoom 417, 1054 JR Amsterdam, Netherlands

picks.name: 4BeerTemple
picks.whyItMadeTheList: Founded by the same team behind Craft & Draft, BeerTemple was one of Amsterdam's first bars to champion American craft beer. Located centrally, it offers a warm, inviting atmosphere with a focus on high-quality US imports, alongside an excellent selection of Dutch and European brews.
picks.whatToOrder: Any IPA from a renowned US brewery on tap
picks.insiderTip: Can get quite busy, especially on weekends. Arrive earlier in the evening if you want a good seat.
picks.redditQuote: “If you're into American craft, BeerTemple is your spot. They always have some insane IPAs from the states, even better than some places back home.”
picks.mapQuery: BeerTemple, Nieuwezijds Voorburgwal 250, 1012 RR Amsterdam, Netherlands

picks.name: 5In de Wildeman
picks.whyItMadeTheList: A true classic, In de Wildeman is a historic brown café with a vast selection of Belgian and Dutch beers, both on tap and in bottles. It's an unpretentious, friendly spot popular with locals and tourists alike, perfect for a relaxed evening of serious beer tasting in a timeless setting.
picks.whatToOrder: Any classic Belgian Trappist ale or a local barleywine
picks.insiderTip: They don't serve food, but you can bring your own snacks or pick up some cheese and sausage from a nearby shop.
picks.redditQuote: “Wildeman is legendary. No music, no fuss, just incredible beer and a great atmosphere to actually talk to people. Love that place.”
picks.mapQuery: Beer Tasting Room In The Wildeman, Kolksteeg 3, 1012 PT Amsterdam, Netherlands

picks.name: 6Café Arendsnest
picks.whyItMadeTheList: Overlooking the picturesque Prinsengracht canal, Café Arendsnest prides itself on exclusively serving Dutch beers. With over 50 taps and more than 100 bottles, it's the ultimate destination to explore the breadth and quality of Holland's brewing scene, from established names to obscure microbreweries.
picks.whatToOrder: A flight of various Dutch craft beers to sample different styles
picks.insiderTip: Grab a spot on the small outdoor terrace if the weather is good for excellent canal views while you sip.
picks.redditQuote: “Arendsnest is a gem if you want to dive deep into Dutch beers. They have everything, and the canal view is just icing on the cake.”
picks.mapQuery: Proeflokaal Arendsnest, Herengracht 90, 1015 BS Amsterdam, Netherlands

picks.name: 7Butcher's Tears
picks.whyItMadeTheList: Butcher's Tears operates out of an industrial space in Amsterdam Zuid, focusing on producing small-batch, often experimental, and highly unique beers. Their taproom offers a minimalist yet inviting environment, attracting those who appreciate sophisticated and unconventional brews.
picks.whatToOrder: Their seasonal sour or a farmhouse ale, always something different
picks.insiderTip: Check their website or social media for opening hours, as they can sometimes vary. It's a bit off the beaten path, adding to its allure.
picks.redditQuote: “If you're tired of the mainstream, Butcher's Tears is where it's at. Super creative beers, not for everyone, but if you get it, you get it.”
picks.mapQuery: Butcher's Tears, Karperweg 45, 1075 LB Amsterdam, Netherlands

picks.name: 8Brouwerij Troost (Westergas)
picks.whyItMadeTheList: One of Amsterdam's larger and more popular brewpubs, Brouwerij Troost at Westergasfabriek offers a spacious and lively environment perfect for groups. They brew a wide range of accessible beers and serve excellent gastropub-style food, making it ideal for both beer enthusiasts and casual diners.
picks.whatToOrder: Troost Weizen and their famous burgers
picks.insiderTip: Located within the Westergas cultural park, it's a great spot to combine with a stroll through the park or visiting a market/event.
picks.redditQuote: “Troost Westergas is always a good time. Great beers, solid food, and the perfect spot to hang out with friends in Westerpark.”
picks.mapQuery: Brouwerij Troost Westergas, Pazzanistraat 27, 1014 DB Amsterdam, Netherlands

picks.name: 9Café Gollem (Raamsteeg)
picks.whyItMadeTheList: With several locations across the city, the original Café Gollem on Raamsteeg is a cozy, atmospheric spot renowned for its incredible selection of Belgian beers. Dimly lit and full of character, it's a perfect retreat for savoring rare and classic Belgian brews in a traditional setting.
picks.whatToOrder: Any obscure Belgian strong dark ale from their bottle list
picks.insiderTip: Don't be afraid to ask the bartender for recommendations; their knowledge of Belgian beers is extensive.
picks.redditQuote: “Gollem is my favorite cozy spot for a proper Belgian beer. Feels like stepping back in time, and the beer menu is endless.”
picks.mapQuery: Cafe Gollem Raamsteeg, Raamsteeg 4, 1012 VZ Amsterdam, Netherlands

picks.name: 10De Biertuin
picks.whyItMadeTheList: De Biertuin, meaning 'The Beer Garden,' lives up to its name with a massive outdoor terrace perfect for enjoying good weather and great beer. They offer a solid selection of craft beers, both local and international, alongside a menu of hearty, unpretentious food like rotisserie chicken and ribs.
picks.whatToOrder: A classic pilsner or a local IPA with their half rotisserie chicken
picks.insiderTip: It's very popular on sunny days, so try to arrive early to snag a good table on the terrace.
picks.redditQuote: “De Biertuin is fantastic in the summer. Great vibe, good food, and they always have a solid beer list without being too snobby.”
picks.mapQuery: De Biertuin East, Linnaeusstraat 29, 1093 EE Amsterdam, Netherlands

picks.name: 11Walhalla Brouwerij & Proeflokaal
picks.whyItMadeTheList: Walhalla Brouwerij draws inspiration from Norse mythology, creating imaginative beers with names like Loki and Thor. Their spacious taproom in Amsterdam-Noord is a relaxed place to enjoy their creative concoctions, often featuring unique ingredients and bold flavor profiles. They regularly host events and food trucks.
picks.whatToOrder: Loki (IPA) or a seasonal special like the Heimdall Hazy IPA
picks.insiderTip: Check their website for brewery tours and special events. They often have new releases or collaborations.
picks.redditQuote: “Walhalla in Noord is such a cool spot. Love the mythology theme, and their beers are always interesting. Loki is my absolute favorite IPA right now.”
picks.mapQuery: Walhalla Brewery & Taproom, Asterweg 2, 1031 HN Amsterdam, Netherlands

picks.name: 12Gebrouwen door Vrouwen Bar
picks.whyItMadeTheList: Founded by two sisters, Gebrouwen door Vrouwen (Brewed by Women) has a vibrant bar in the popular De Pijp area. Their beers are known for being approachable, often fruity and light, but always full of flavor. The bar itself is colorful and lively, attracting a diverse crowd.
picks.whatToOrder: Bloesem (Blond Ale with Elderflower) or Gin Weizen
picks.insiderTip: They also offer a small menu of bar bites that pair well with their beers. It's a great place to start an evening in De Pijp.
picks.redditQuote: “Gebrouwen door Vrouwen bar is just a really happy place! Their Gin Weizen is surprisingly good, and the whole vibe is super welcoming.”
picks.mapQuery: Brewed by Women BAR, Jan Pieter Heijestraat 119D, hs, 1054 MD Amsterdam, Netherlands

faq.question: What is the average price for a craft beer in Amsterdam?
faq.answer: The average price for a pint or a 0.3L/0.4L glass of craft beer in Amsterdam typically ranges from €6 to €9 ($6.50 to $9.70).

faq.question: Are there many breweries in Amsterdam that offer tours?
faq.answer: Yes, Brouwerij 't IJ and Brouwerij Troost offer tours. Check their websites for schedules and book in advance.

faq.question: Which neighborhood is best for craft beer hopping in Amsterdam?
faq.answer: De Pijp and Centrum (city center) are excellent. De Pijp has modern taprooms like Craft & Draft; Centrum has historic brown cafés like In de Wildeman and BeerTemple.

faq.question: Can I find non-alcoholic craft beer options in Amsterdam?
faq.answer: Yes, most dedicated craft beer bars and breweries now offer quality NA options. Just ask the bartender.

faq.question: Is it customary to tip in Amsterdam craft beer bars?
faq.answer: Tipping is not mandatory but appreciated. Leaving a few euros or rounding up is common; 5-10% for larger groups.

faq.question: Are Amsterdam's craft beer bars dog-friendly?
faq.answer: Many are, especially those with outdoor terraces. Look for 'honden toegestaan' (dogs allowed) signs or check with the venue first.
